subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: If A, B are events with P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4 and P(A ∩ B) = 0.3, find the probability that (i) A does not occur (ii) neither A nor B occurs.

mark_split.label: (ii) Neither A nor B is the complement of A ∪ B

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the probability that A does not occur, and that neither A nor B occurs — which set each one is, and the numbers.
insider_note: "Neither A nor B" is the complement of "A or B", so it is 1 − P(A ∪ B). Students who write 1 − P(A ∩ B) get 0.7 and lose both marks of part (ii).

steps.label: (i) A does not occur
steps.margin_note: First mark. "A does not occur" is Aᶜ: 1 − 0.5 = 0.5.
steps.memory_tip: 'A does not occur' is Aᶜ, so 1 − P(A) = 0.5.

recall.must_convey: That the probability A does not occur is P(Aᶜ) = 1 − P(A) = 0.5.
accept: A does not occur is the complement, one minus point five equals point five
P of A complement is 1 minus 0.5 which is 0.5
the chance A fails is half
A jaragakapovadam ante A complement, 1 minus 0.5, 0.5

steps.why: An event and its complement together are certain, so their probabilities add to 1.

steps.label: (ii) Neither A nor B = (A ∪ B)ᶜ
steps.margin_note: Second mark. "Neither A nor B" means A does not occur AND B does not occur: Aᶜ ∩ Bᶜ, which is the complement of A ∪ B. Writing this identity is the mark.
steps.memory_tip: 'Neither A nor B' is Aᶜ ∩ Bᶜ = (A ∪ B)ᶜ — the complement of the UNION, not of the intersection.

lines.text: P(Aᶜ ∩ Bᶜ) = P((A ∪ B)ᶜ) = 1 − P(A ∪ B)

recall.must_convey: That "neither A nor B" is Aᶜ ∩ Bᶜ, the complement of A ∪ B, so its probability is 1 − P(A ∪ B).
accept: neither A nor B is A complement intersection B complement which is the complement of A union B so one minus P of A union B
neither means the complement of the union
not A and not B equals one minus P A union B
neither A nor B ante A union B complement, 1 minus P of union
heard_as: one minus P A union B

steps.why: De Morgan's law: the complement of "at least one" is "none". That converts the question into one about the union, which the addition theorem can give.
common_mistakes: Writing neither A nor B = 1 − P(A ∩ B).
Multiplying P(Aᶜ)·P(Bᶜ) — that needs independence, which is not given.

steps.label: Find P(A ∪ B) and finish
steps.memory_tip: Addition theorem gives P(A ∪ B) = 0.6, then 1 − 0.6 = 0.4.

lines.text: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B)

accept: the union is point five plus point four minus point three which is point six so neither is one minus point six equals point four
addition theorem gives 0.6 and one minus that is 0.4
P A union B is 0.6, neither is 0.4

steps.why: The addition theorem is the only route to the union from the three given numbers; the complement then finishes the question.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to subtract P(A ∩ B) and getting 0.9, then 0.1.
Stopping at P(A ∪ B) = 0.6 as the answer to (ii).
